_about: Raw JSON-RPC (stdio, newline-delimited) against claims_server.py (a MOCK of the platform team's server). 'message' is verbatim from capture_wire.py; 'annotations' are hand-written, one per top-level field.
model_call: The model call happens in mcp_agent.py (the host/client, Groq), between tool results and the next turn; it does NOT happen in the MCP server or anywhere on this wire.

annotations.jsonrpc: JSON-RPC 2.0 version tag; required on every message, always the string '2.0'.
annotations.id: Client-chosen request id (1). The server must echo it in its reply so the client can match reply to request.
annotations.method: 'initialize' = the mandatory first request; opens the session and negotiates protocol.

params.protocolVersion: Newest MCP spec revision the client speaks; server answers with the one it will use.
params.capabilities: Features the client offers the server (sampling, roots, ...). {} = none offered.
params.clientInfo: Who is calling: name/version, for server-side logs only.

annotations.jsonrpc: JSON-RPC 2.0 version tag; required on every message, always the string '2.0'.
annotations.id: Echo of request id 1: this is the reply to initialize.

result.capabilities: What the server can do: tools (listChanged=false: its tool set won't change mid-session), plus prompts/resources it advertises but doesn't use here.
result.serverInfo: Server's self-declared name ('claims-system') and version (empty string).

annotations.jsonrpc: JSON-RPC 2.0 version tag; required on every message, always the string '2.0'.
annotations.method: 'notifications/initialized' = client says handshake done. No 'id' field: a notification, so no reply is sent or expected.

annotations.jsonrpc: JSON-RPC 2.0 version tag; required on every message, always the string '2.0'.
annotations.method: 'tools/list' = discovery. This is the call mcp_agent.py uses to learn what tools exist; no params needed.

tools.description:
Look up the current status of one claim by claim number (CLM-YYYY-nnnnnn).
    Returns JSON with status, policy form/edition, date of loss and claimed amount.
tools.name: get_claim_status

tools.description:
Fetch the adjuster note history for one claim by claim number
    (CLM-YYYY-nnnnnn). Returns a JSON list of dated notes, newest first; the
    claimant's name is redacted.
tools.name: get_adjuster_notes

annotations.jsonrpc: JSON-RPC 2.0 version tag; required on every message, always the string '2.0'.

result.tools: One entry per tool. Each: name (what the model will call), description (the docstring -- the model reads this as a prompt), inputSchema (JSON Schema for arguments; becomes the model's tool 'parameters'), outputSchema (SDK-generated schema of structuredContent; the model never needs it).

annotations.jsonrpc: JSON-RPC 2.0 version tag; required on every message, always the string '2.0'.
annotations.method: 'tools/call' = execute one tool. The only message here that runs claim-lookup code.

params.name: Which tool to run -- must match a name from tools/list.
params.arguments: Values conforming to that tool's inputSchema; in the agent these are what the model generated.

annotations.jsonrpc: JSON-RPC 2.0 version tag; required on every message, always the string '2.0'.

result.content: List of content blocks returned to the model; here one text block whose 'text' is the claim JSON (as a string).
result.isError: false = tool succeeded. Tool failures come back as isError=true inside a normal result, NOT as a JSON-RPC 'error' -- so the model can read and react to them.
result.structuredContent: Same data in machine-readable form (SDK wraps the string in {result: ...}); the agent uses 'content', not this.
